title: Depth-zero AC languages have shallow tree circuits
statement: If a language over Boolean strings is recognized by a well-formed family of Boolean circuits of polynomial size and depth at most a constant times $(\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1)^0$ on inputs of length $n$, then it is recognized by a family of Boolean circuit trees of polynomial size and depth at most a constant times $(\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1)^0$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language over Boolean strings
$L$ has a well-formed circuit family of polynomial size
That family has polylogarithmic depth with exponent $0$
